title: One payee, another organization's money: fiscal sponsors named on contract notices
question: Which City payees were paid as the fiscal sponsor of a separately named project, and what happened to the project when the sponsor stopped being paid?
finding: 41 sponsor-and-project pairs are written into the contractor line of City contract notices: the payee is the sponsor, the money is for the project. The sponsors named most often: San Francisco Study Center Inc. (6 projects); Filipino-American Development Foundation (4 projects); St James Infirmary (3 projects); Somarts (2 projects). In 4 pairs the sponsor was last paid before fiscal 2026: St James Infirmary for Compton'S Transgender Cultural District (sponsor last paid fiscal 2024; not paid under this name; a payee with a like name, The Transgender District, was first paid in fiscal 2024 ($3.2 million since)); San Francisco Parks Alliance for Urban Sprouts (sponsor last paid fiscal 2025; the project has never been paid in its own name); St James Infirmary for Transgender Gender Variant Intersex Ju (sponsor last paid fiscal 2024; the project became a City payee in its own name in fiscal 2022); St James Infirmary for Transgender Cultural District (sponsor last paid fiscal 2024; not paid under this name; a payee with a like name, The Transgender District, was first paid in fiscal 2024 ($3.2 million since)).
how: The contractor line of every contract notice is read for the words "fiscal sponsor of", "fiscal sponsor for", "f.s." or "fiscally sponsored by". The name before is taken as the sponsor and the name after as the project (or the reverse for "sponsored by"); both are tied to the Controller's payee names as in the first screen. Payments to each are the Controller's payment file since fiscal 2019.
limits: Fiscal sponsorship is an ordinary arrangement: a project without its own tax exemption is paid through an established charity, which holds the money and usually keeps a fee. It matters here because the payment file shows only the sponsor, so a sponsor's City total includes money it passed on, and a sponsor that fails takes its projects' funds with it. The notices give no amounts by project; grants that never needed an elected official's approval have no notice and are not seen. A project name that could not be tied to a payee name may still be paid under another spelling.
